title: Profile health scoring, staleness indicator and gated auto-refresh for verified performance profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Customers rely on Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) when pinning model versions. Profiles degrade over time as hardware, kernels, or model weights change. We currently publish profiles manually and lack a clear, consumer-facing signal for profile freshness or health. This ticket defines a product/ops flow to compute a profile health score, surface a staleness indicator in the Console/API, and implement a gated auto-refresh pipeline (canary micro-bench + human approval) to republish profiles when needed.
background: Existing verified profiles are static artifacts in the catalog. Teams have observed regressions when runtime kernels are updated or when new quantized variants are introduced. Support requests surface ambiguous guidance ("is this profile still reliable?"). Engineering has prototype telemetry (perf-ci feeds) but no product surface to act on it.
acceptance_criteria: Add a 'profile_health_score' (0-100) derived from recent telemetry: median P95 latency delta vs published, throughput delta, and token-unit cost variance
Expose 'freshness' as: FRESH / STALE / EXPIRED in Redwood Console model catalog and via GET /profiles/{id} API
Define staleness thresholds and automated tags: STALE if health_score < 75 or >10% regression on P95, EXPIRED after 90 days without successful verification runs

Implement a gated auto-refresh pipeline: trigger micro-bench canary, run full verification bundle if canary passes, create Draft profile and assign to profile-steward for review, auto-publish on steward approval
Add dashboard panel with historical health score trend for each profile and alerting rule when score drops below 70 (PagerDuty + Slack channel #perf-profiles)
Document the flow in Confluence (Profile Health Playbook) with links to the verification CI and rollback runbook
Include end-to-end test to validate API and Console rendering of freshness tags in QA environment
implementation_steps: Define health_score formula with Research: weight P95 delta (50%), throughput delta (30%), cost variance (20%)
Wire perf-ci telemetry into the profile-store processing job to compute rolling 7-day metrics
Add new DB column: health_score and freshness_state (string) to profile records (DB migrations managed by infra)
Build micro-bench canary job (small sample load) and integrate with existing verification pipeline
Create publish workflow: canary -> full verification -> Draft profile -> steward approval -> Publish
Console: add freshness pill and tooltip with last_verified_at and score breakdown
API: extend GET /profiles and list endpoints to include health_score, freshness_state, last_verified_at, and verification_run_id
Setup dashboards/alerts in Grafana and link to PagerDuty escalation policy
Write PRD + runbook and schedule product review with Platform and Research teams
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy telemetry may produce false positives. Mitigation: use rolling-window median and require >2 independent verification runs before state flips

Risk: Auto-refresh could regress production apps if verification is insufficient. Mitigation: keep human steward approval in the loop for major profile deltas, add canary shadow traffic option for critical customers
Risk: Extra verification runs increase infra cost. Mitigation: schedule low-cost canaries during off-peak and only run full verification when canary passes
Risk: Console clutter / customer confusion. Mitigation: include clear tooltip language and link to playbook explaining implications of FRESH/STALE/EXPIRED
metrics_to_track: Number of profile refresh workflows triggered per week
Time from canary success to publish (target < 48h with steward approval)
Number of customer tickets mentioning stale/incorrect profiles (target reduction 50% in Q2)
False-positive refresh rate (refreshes that roll back within 7 days)
